q: Can you find how many games he increased by with his drops and adds and waiver claims? Seems like he nailed that last week
short: I'm assuming 'he' is you: your 4 add/drop moves last week (Nov 2 to 8) put players on your roster who logged about 6 games, but I can't compute a clean net games gain because the data has no per-game schedule for dropped players.
answer:
I'm reading 'he' as you (Garebears). If you meant another manager, tell me who and I'll rerun it.

Last week you made 4 free agent add/drops and no waiver claims: Wiggins for Pippen Jr. (Nov 2), Zubac for Poeltl (Nov 4), Collins for Gordon (Nov 7), and Bridges for Grimes (Nov 7). The lineup logs show your added players appeared in about 6 games for you: Wiggins 4 (Nov 2, 4, 5, 8), Zubac 1 (Nov 7), Collins 1 (Nov 8) and Bridges 0 logged.

On the drop side, Pippen Jr. gave you 0 games (he was out), Poeltl gave 1 (Nov 4, before the swap), Gordon gave 2 before he was dropped, and Grimes gave 3 before he was dropped. The logs only record games while a player was on your roster, so I cannot see how many games the dropped players played after leaving. That means a true net games gained figure is not available, only a rough read.

Rough read: the swaps added about 6 games from the new players. The real gain depends on what the drops would have played, which the data does not show. Wiggins for Pippen Jr. was clearly the big win, since it turned 0 games into 4. Grimes is listed OUT, which makes dropping him sensible, but Bridges having nothing logged was a miss.

I did not use web searches since this is purely about your own roster history. Confidence is moderate: the add side comes straight from the logs, the drop side is incomplete.
